architecture.title: The sovereign hotel agent on two Sparks — every piece from this week, wired together
architecture.caption: Spark B serves the fine-tuned router (Module 09's LoRA on Qwen3-4B, served as in Module 13). Spark A serves the agent's brain (Qwen3.6 agent-ready recipe, Module 05), the LiteLLM gateway (Module 08) and an OpenShell sandbox (Module 15) running the NAT agent (Module 14). The sandbox has two ways out: inference.local (routed to the gateway's agent-brain alias) and the gateway itself for the router tool. Nothing leaves the two Sparks.

sequence.title: Lab 20-3 — the 'smoke' scenario, captured on the laptop stand-in
sequence.caption: Real NAT 1.9 run through a real LiteLLM 1.89 proxy; both aliases fell back to gemma4:12b on the laptop because no Spark was serving. The order is enforced by the system prompt and checked by the acceptance judge: route first, then act.

charts.title: Acceptance checks passed per scenario (lab 20-3, laptop stand-in, two runs identical)
charts.caption: The one failure is Module 13's finding again: the prompt-only stand-in router marks a normal Thai request urgent. The fine-tuned router on Spark B is what has to fix it.

charts.title: Memory each Spark reserves for vLLM (lab 20-1, arithmetic)
charts.caption: --gpu-memory-utilization 0.4 on A (Module 05's agent recipe) and 0.3 on B. Spark B keeps enough room to train the next LoRA adapter while the current one serves.
